title: How the individual commands were counted
content:
How the individual commands were counted

Read Instructions · Instructions index · Beyond the Torah · Counting and classification guide

Counting, classification and open questions

A count records what the catalogue includes; a classification interprets the relationship between passages. These are separate decisions. Read the full classification definitions.

Historical setting and uncertainty should be recorded separately. A historical commission may be clear in scope; uncertainty concerns what has not yet been established. Do not force either into the four theological marks. Wider coverage and further research.

The current Saints Translation text of Genesis through Deuteronomy, as preserved in the linked staging chapter pages and the accompanying source snapshot. This is a text-based editorial catalogue, not a number stated by Scripture and not an independent audit of the translation against every Hebrew and Greek manuscript.

1,223 individually indexed requirements in the main catalogue: 895 covenant laws, procedures and general exhortations; 324 personal or historical instructions; and 4 creation commissions. Supplement M contains 30 separately identified Moses instructions; supplement F contains 11 foreign-recipient instructions.

Counting rules

  • Count a distinguishable duty, prohibition, procedural action or personal commission as one requirement. Keep its original recipient, circumstances, exceptions and qualifications attached to it.
  • Count the same requirement once when it is repeated. Link repeated passages to the existing command ID. Distinct ritual procedures, recipients, objects or historical occasions can have separate requirements even when their verbs are similar.
  • Count separately expressed positive duties and prohibitions separately when each supplies a distinguishable operative requirement. General commands to obey, fear or love God remain general exhortations; they do not replace the detailed laws.
  • Treat dimensions, quantities, materials, dates, eligible persons and lists of species as qualifications of the action they specify. Do not create a new command for every number, noun or grammatical verb. A specified construction or inspection can therefore remain one requirement; separately prescribed actions, such as slaughtering, washing and applying blood, receive separate entries.
  • Include God's direct speech, instructions attributed to Him through Moses, the covenant law Moses teaches as God's law, and the narrated instructions of divine messengers. Include the ancestral household and creation commissions because the requested scope begins in Genesis. Deuteronomy 1:3 and 4:5 supply the book's divine-law framing.
  • Keep personal and event-specific instructions separate from covenant laws and general exhortations. A command to Noah, Moses, a particular army or the original sanctuary artisans is not automatically a command to every reader.
  • Keep separately identified operational directions spoken by Moses, without a stated divine attribution for that particular direction, in supplement M. This classification does not declare them ungodly; it makes the evidential distinction visible. Keep divine instructions to foreign recipients outside the ancestral household in supplement F. Neither supplement is included in the main total.
  • Do not manufacture new commands from permissions, promises, predictions, prayers addressed to God, human advice, narrated customs or records of completed obedience. Do not treat every occurrence of 'shall' as an imperative. Legislative penalties directed to human administration are included; divine threats and consequences are not converted into extra human duties.
  • Introductory formulas such as 'say to Israel' normally introduce the command that follows rather than adding another command to its count. Substantive commissions to deliver a particular message, teach the law or make a particular public declaration are retained.
  • The summaries and numerical IDs are editorial aids. Read the linked verse range and surrounding chapter for the full condition. This catalogue records original requirements; it does not assign new Fulfilled or Transformed judgments or make all ancient requirements binding on Christians.

Decisions that affect the total

Text and numbering

  • Saints follows Greek/LXX wording and numbering in these pages. References therefore follow the actual Saints verse anchors, including Leviticus 5:20–26, the Numbers 17 divisions and Deuteronomy 23:1. Gaps in a chapter's displayed numbering are not filled with verses imported from a different edition.
  • Genesis 4:7 ('be still'), Exodus 13:13 (firstborn donkey), Exodus 22:27 ('gods'), Leviticus 19:26 ('on the mountains') and 19:27 (the haircut term) are retained according to the current Saints wording. Their Hebrew/Greek interpretation is not settled merely by assigning an entry number.
  • Exodus 12:9 prohibits boiling the Passover, while the current Saints Deuteronomy 16:7 says 'boil it, and roast it'. Both passages remain visible; the catalogue does not silently rewrite either or assert a harmonization.
  • The current Leviticus 14:39 wording says the house lesion has 'not spread' before the next prescribed action. The catalogue uses neutral procedure wording and preserves the source; a separate translation audit would be needed to settle that textual issue.
  • The scope and language of ancient judgments, slavery, war, marriage and ritual restrictions remain attached to their original passages. Their inclusion is a historical record of the text, not a modern instruction to carry them out.

Scope of the result: All 187 chapters are represented in the audit. The total is reproducible from the included annotations and counting rules. Decisions about separating actions, grouping repeated requirements, divine attribution and textual readings remain editorial; the total should not be advertised as the single universally fixed number of God's commands.

Chapter audit

The number of IDs cited in a chapter is not a new total. An ID may occur in several chapters and books.
